Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of requests so we can follow up with a concrete reserved-capacity proposal: 

Summary from call:
- Target initial monthly throughput: ~50M tokens/month (production footprint after pilot).
- Peak behavior: short bursts during processing windows (top burst ~20 concurrent inference requests, P95 latency target <200ms).
- Primary models: a trimmed LLM for extraction/ranking plus a larger model for long-form summaries (quality matters for the latter).
- Commercial target: move to dedicated/reserved lanes in Q1 if economics line up.

As next steps, can you confirm two things so we can size properly:
1) Expected monthly token volume band this quarter (choose one): 10–25M | 25–50M | 50–100M.
2) Budget range for dedicated inference (monthly committed spend) — a rough band is fine.

Ben and Marissa — can you sketch 2–3 reserve configurations and a first-pass $/1M-token estimate for BlueStream once Elaine confirms the bands? Please include GPU family tradeoffs (H100 vs A100 vs cheaper L4-like variants) and any obvious quality tradeoffs.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (pricing sketch and reserve SKU definitions)

Elaine — appreciate a quick reply here so we can get a tailored commitment proposal out this week.

Thanks,

Putting together two concrete reserve configurations and the math based on Elaine’s bands. High-level notes up-front: quality-sensitive long-form summaries favor H100/FP16 or A100/FP16 with minimal quantization. For cost-first extraction-only workloads, we can push quantized L4-style instances which materially lower $/1M tokens but may slightly affect top-end output quality.

Option 1 — Conservative (quality-first):
- HW: 3x H100 (reserved pool), software: FP16 inference, minimal quantization for summary model.
- Estimated sustained throughput (combined): ~380 tokens/sec total (burstable to ~520 tokens/sec for short windows).
- Monthly capacity estimate (sustained util ~60%): ~680M tokens/month aggregate capacity; realistic usable tokens (headroom for spikes) ~400–500M.
- Committed pricing: $ estimate = $29,500/month for the 3x H100 reserved lane (includes baseline infra, support SLA).
- Implied unit econ: $29,500 / 50M tokens = $590 / 1M tokens at 50M — but since capacity is shared and utilization matters, with a 50–100M band your effective $/1M (at 80M realized) =~ $369 / 1M. Lower than pay-as-you-go but higher than heavily-quantized lanes.

Option 2 — Balanced (cost + quality):
- HW: 4x A100 (reserved), mixed FP16 + targeted quantization for extraction model only.
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~320 tokens/sec (burst to ~420).
- Monthly capacity est (sustained util 65%): ~540M tokens/month; realistic usable ~300–400M.
- Committed pricing: $ estimate = $10,800/month for the 4x A100 reserved lane.
- Implied unit econ: at 50M tokens = $216 / 1M tokens; at 80M tokens = $135 / 1M tokens.

Option 3 — Cost-optimized (quantized, lower quality tail):
- HW: 6x L4-like instances (aggressive int8 quantization), optimized runtime.
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~300 tokens/sec (latency slightly higher for some long requests).
- Monthly capacity est: ~500M tokens/month usable.
- Committed pricing: $ estimate = $6,200/month.
- Implied unit econ: at 50M tokens = $124 / 1M tokens; at 80M tokens = $78 / 1M tokens.

Notes on assumptions and how to tighten:
- These are committed-reserved SKU sketches; actual unit $/1M varies heavily with utilization and model selection. The headline takeaway: you can hit Elaine’s $/1M target range (given the $6k–$12k budget) with a cost-optimized reserve or a balanced A100 pool assuming ~80M tokens/month realized.
- H100 gives clear quality headroom but at materially higher committed spend.
- We should run a short pilot on a smaller reserved lane (e.g., 1x H100 + 2x L4 lanes) to observe real token mix and effective throughput; then convert to a larger reserved bundle with a ramp schedule.

Attachments: gpu_benchmark_20261214.csv (raw perf numbers used for the calc), redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf

Action suggestion: I’ll prepare two formal SKUs (Balanced and Cost-optimized) with explicit monthly commit, uplift discounts, and conversion path to H100 if BlueStream wants to upgrade.

—Ben
